title: Pause on speed cameras pending Region agreement
subtitle: Council also asked the province to cut camera fines and directed staff on infrastructure security and a labour matter.
overview: Council voted to pause current and future automated speed enforcement (ASE) camera installations on City-owned roads. The pause lasts until Council approves a Memorandum of Understanding with the Region of Waterloo, or another operating model. That agreement would cover revenue sharing and let Council change camera operating times. The motion passed as amended {{vote:m1}}.

An amendment removed wording that had exempted locations already approved, so the pause covers cameras already planned as well. It passed {{vote:m2}}. Staff also heard that the Region is working on its approved 2024 locations now. Council directed staff to report on whether the City could become an ASE provider, including through an external service provider. Council also asked the province to reduce the fines set under Ontario Regulation 355/22, which are roughly double the earlier fine amounts.

After a recess, Council met in closed session. It then directed staff to proceed with initiatives to reduce risks to the security of physical and digital City infrastructure. Any further budget needs will go to the 2025 budget process. Council also directed staff to proceed with a labour relations matter, as set out in a report from October 21, 2024.

decisions.detail: Council paused current and future ASE installations on City roads until it approves an agreement with the Region of Waterloo or another operating model covering revenue sharing and camera operating times {{vote:m1}}.
Council amended the pause so it applies to current and future installations, removing the exemption for locations already approved {{vote:m2}}.
Staff were directed to investigate and report back on whether the City could be appointed an ASE provider, including external service provider options.
Council asked the Ontario government to amend Ontario Regulation 355/22 so set fines are similar to those in section 128(14) of the Highway Traffic Act.
Staff were directed to proceed with initiatives to address risks to physical and digital City infrastructure, with any extra budget needs going to the 2025 budget process.
Staff were directed to proceed in accordance with the in-camera direction in report COR-2024-469 on a labour relations matter.
